items.en: Excuse me, where is the metro?
The bank is next to the pharmacy.
Does this street go to the center?
There are many mountains in Georgia.
The Mtkvari river flows through Tbilisi.
There are many trees in the forest.
The lake water was very cold.
In summer we went to the mountains.
The sky over the sea is very blue.
There are high mountains in Svaneti.
The nature here is very beautiful.
Tbilisi is the capital of Georgia.
Batumi is on the Black Sea.
Kutaisi is in the west of Georgia.
Mtskheta is a very old city.
There are many tourists in Batumi in summer.
The center of Kutaisi is small and calm.
It's twenty minutes from Tbilisi to Mtskheta.
The meat and the garlic are on the table.
Mom made a very tasty lobio.
The child is afraid of the dark.
I was nervous before the exam.
I sent the photos to my friend.
My family is in this photo.
In the evening I watch videos.
Come to our place on Saturday!
Let's meet at the metro at seven.
Rugby is very popular in Georgia.
In summer my child swims in the sea.

ka-a2-dir.title: Directions
ka-a2-dir.explanation: Directions: პირდაპირ (straight ahead), მარცხნივ (to the left), მარჯვნივ (to the right), ახლოს (near), შორს (far), გვერდით (next to), წინ (in front), უკან (behind). Start politely with უკაცრავად ('excuse me'). For distances, ხუთი წუთია ('it's five minutes') is enough.
ka-a2-dir.fact: Many Tbilisi streets are named after writers and poets, and the main avenue is named after the medieval poet Shota Rustaveli.

dialogue.en: Excuse me, where is the station?

ka-a2-nature.title: Nature
ka-a2-nature.explanation: Nature words: მთა (mountain), მდინარე (river), ტბა (lake), ტყე (forest), ზღვა (sea), ცა (sky), ხე (tree), ყვავილი (flower). 'In the mountains' is მთებში, 'by the sea' ზღვაზე (literally 'on the sea'). The Caucasus is კავკასიონი.
ka-a2-nature.fact: Georgia's highest mountain is Shkhara (შხარა), at about 5,200 metres, in the region of Svaneti on the border with Russia.

dialogue.en: Do you like the mountains or the sea?
The mountains! In summer I went to Svaneti.

ka-a2-cities.title: Georgian Cities
ka-a2-cities.explanation: Georgia's main cities: თბილისი (the capital), ქუთაისი (in the west), ბათუმი (on the Black Sea), რუსთავი (near Tbilisi), and the ancient town of მცხეთა. City names take the usual endings: ქუთაისში ('in Kutaisi'), ბათუმიდან ('from Batumi'). Remember the genitive for 'of': ქუთაისის ცენტრი ('the center of Kutaisi').
ka-a2-cities.fact: Mtskheta, just north of Tbilisi, was Georgia's ancient capital and is one of the oldest continuously inhabited towns in the country.

dialogue.en: Yes, it's a very beautiful city.

ka-a2-cook.title: Cooking: Step by Step
ka-a2-cook.explanation: Recipes use the imperative, which looks like the past 'you' form: აიღე (take), დაჭერი (chop), დაამატე (add). Ingredients: ხორცი (meat), ხახვი (onion), ნიორი (garlic), მარილი (salt), კარაქი (butter), ფქვილი (flour), კვერცხი (egg).
ka-a2-cook.fact: Walnuts appear in a remarkable number of Georgian dishes, ground into sauces for vegetables, chicken and fish.

dialogue.en: What do we need for lobio?

ka-a2-feel.title: Feelings
ka-a2-feel.explanation: Describe feelings with the verb 'to be': ბედნიერი ვარ ('I am happy'), სევდიანი ხარ? ('are you sad?'), დაღლილი ვარ ('I am tired'). Other useful words: კმაყოფილი (pleased), ნერვიული (nervous). Feelings can also be inverted verbs: მეშინია ('I'm afraid'), მიხარია ('I'm glad').
ka-a2-feel.fact: მიხარია ('I'm glad') is built from the same root as სიხარული ('joy') and works like მიყვარს, with the person in the dative.

dialogue.en: I'm tired; I had a lot of work.

ka-a2-tech.title: Phones and Computers
ka-a2-tech.explanation: Technology words are mostly international: კომპიუტერი, ინტერნეტი, ტელეფონი, ფოტო, ვიდეო. Useful verbs: გავგზავნე (I sent), გავუგზავნე (I sent to him/her), მან გაუგზავნა (he/she sent to someone). 'Online' is often just ინტერნეტით ('via the internet').
ka-a2-tech.fact: Phones and computers have a Georgian keyboard layout, so typing in Mkhedruli is easy on any device.

dialogue.en: Did Nino send the photos to Mom?
Yes, she sent them this morning.

ka-a2-invite.title: Inviting and Accepting
ka-a2-invite.explanation: Invite with მოდი ჩვენთან ('come to our place') or წავიდეთ … ('let's go …'). Accept with სიამოვნებით ('with pleasure') or კარგი იდეაა ('good idea'). To decline politely: სამწუხაროდ, ვერ მოვალ ('unfortunately I can't come'). ვერ is the 'can't' negative: ვერ მოვალ means 'I won't be able to come'.
ka-a2-invite.fact: Georgian has two words for 'not': არ (doesn't / won't) and ვერ (can't / won't be able to). არ მოვალ means 'I won't come'; ვერ მოვალ means 'I can't come'.

dialogue.en: Come over on Saturday, we're having dinner.

ka-a2-sport.title: Sport
ka-a2-sport.explanation: Sports: ფეხბურთი (football), კალათბურთი (basketball, 'basket-ball'), რაგბი (rugby), ჭიდაობა (wrestling), ცურვა (swimming). 'I play' is ვთამაშობ + the sport in the dative: ფეხბურთს ვთამაშობ. A game is თამაში, a team გუნდი, and 'won' is გაიმარჯვა.
ka-a2-sport.fact: Rugby is one of the most popular sports in Georgia, and the national team regularly plays at the Rugby World Cup.

dialogue.en: Did you watch the game yesterday?
